items.stem: What does the ? operator do when applied to a Result in a function returning Result?

options.text: Returns the error early from the function, otherwise unwraps the Ok value
options.rationale: ? propagates Err via an early return and yields the Ok value on success.

options.text: Converts the Result into an Option
options.rationale: ? keeps the Result flow; it does not change it to Option here.
? never discards the error; it returns it.

items.explanation: ? propagates Err via an early return and yields the Ok value on success.

items.stem: Select TWO true statements about iterator adaptors like map and filter in Rust.

options.text: They are lazy and do nothing until a consumer such as collect or for is used
options.rationale: Adaptors build a pipeline evaluated only when consumed.

options.text: Each adaptor allocates a new Vec immediately
options.rationale: Adaptors are lazy and allocation-free until collected.

options.text: They can be chained and fused by the compiler into efficient code
options.rationale: Chained adaptors compile to tight loops with no per-step allocation.

options.text: filter can change the item type of the iterator
options.rationale: filter keeps the item type; map changes it.

items.explanation: Adaptors build a pipeline evaluated only when consumed.

items.stem: Why define a custom error enum with From implementations in a Rust library?

options.text: To unify different underlying errors behind one type that ? can convert into
options.rationale: From impls let ? auto-convert source errors into the library's error type.

options.text: To make all functions return Option instead of Result
options.rationale: Custom error types are about Result, not Option.

options.text: To force every caller to call unwrap
options.rationale: The goal is the opposite of forcing unwrap.

options.text: To disable the borrow checker for error paths
options.rationale: Error types do not affect borrow checking.

items.explanation: From impls let ? auto-convert source errors into the library's error type.
